artifact.analytic_headline: The sharp minimum-critical-height problem for monic real-rooted degree n polynomials of root diameter D has value (D/2)^n / (2^(n-1) cos(pi/(2n))^n), attained by the endpoint-normalized scaled Chebyshev polynomial. The minimizing critical gap gives an adjacent chord at the same level. Consequently the Erdős path conclusion holds for collinear roots in the open unit disk, and even in the closed unit disk for n>=3

human_understanding_delta: A constrained Chebyshev alternation argument removes the resultant bottleneck and gives the exact answer. After normalizing the extreme roots to -1 and 1, compare the monic root polynomial q with q_*(x)=T_n(r_n x)/(2^(n-1) r_n^n), r_n=cos(pi/(2n)). Both vanish at the endpoints and |q_*|<=C_n=1/(2^(n-1)r_n^n). If every adjacent gap of q had peak above C_n, q-q_* would have the two endpoint zeros plus one zero between each consecutive pair of alternating gap peaks: n distinct zeros despite degree at most n-1. Scaled Chebyshev roots make every gap peak exactly C_n, proving all-degree sharpness. Since C_n<1 for n>=3, the full path conclusion also extends to collinear roots in the closed unit disk: repeated roots give a constant path, while three or more distinct ordered roots make every adjacent gap strictly shorter than diameter two. The prior Chebyshev-Hadamard/resultant theorem remains an independent clean algebraic corollary, and the exact Legendre-Lobatto discriminant recurrence remains a stronger analysis of that secondary route.
